purpose: Sanitized probe of the hosted Jev decision model through OpenRouter, recorded to compare API shape, probability semantics, batching, and latency with this repository's local adapter. Not an accuracy benchmark.

endpoint.auth: Bearer OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the environment; never stored

client.location: Apple Silicon Mac on a residential connection; latency includes network transport
client.concurrency: sequential except the four-request concurrent cadence sample

content_note: All states, events, posts, and boards are synthetic and were written for this probe. No user data.

summary.probability_precision: All returned noul values, probabilities, scores, and confidences carry at most two decimal places; extreme answers are exactly 0 and 1.
summary.repeat_variation: Three identical checkout requests differed by at most 0.02 in any noul; eight identical grid requests returned down-probabilities between 0.86 and 0.89.
summary.question_independence: promo alone 0.99 versus 0.98 in the batch of eight; help 0.79 in both; reversed question order changed no answer by more than 0.01.
summary.criteria_effect_on_this_case: promo without true/false criteria returned 0.98, the same as with criteria; object-valued instructions and criteria were accepted.
summary.confidence_inference: On all 21 choice and score answers in this probe, confidence equals the top-two probability margin within 0.01 rounding. This is an inference from observed values, not a documented formula.
summary.batching: Six posts in one state with one noul per post reproduced the six single-post answers within 0.02 while using 1337 input tokens instead of 2549 across six requests.
summary.cost: cost equals input_tokens times 0.042 per million; output_tokens were nonzero but billed at zero.
summary.errors: Unknown question type and a numeric state root returned HTTP 400 with a discriminated-union validation message listing noul, choice, score, or string, record, array.

promo.instructions: Is the shopper having trouble applying a promo code?

criteria.true: The shopper entered or edited a promo code more than once, saw a promo error, or kept returning to the promo field.
criteria.false: No promo code activity, or a single successful promo apply.

quit.instructions: Is the shopper about to leave checkout without paying?

criteria.true: Long idle gaps late in the form, repeated back navigation, clearing fields, or hovering the close/cart link after errors.
criteria.false: Steady forward progress through the form with recent activity.

fraud.instructions: Does this look like card testing or fraud rather than a normal purchase?

criteria.true: Many different card numbers tried in quick succession, repeated declines, or mismatched billing details changed rapidly.
criteria.false: One or two card attempts with consistent identity details.

ready.instructions: Is the shopper ready to pay right now?

criteria.true: Every required field is complete, payment details entered, and the shopper is on or focusing the pay button.
criteria.false: Required fields are still missing or the shopper is still editing.

shipping.instructions: Is the shopper uncertain about which shipping option to choose?

criteria.true: The shipping option was changed more than once, or the shopper spent a long time on the shipping step, opening delivery details.
criteria.false: Shipping chosen once without revisiting.

help.instructions: Would offering live chat help this shopper complete the purchase?

criteria.true: The shopper hit errors or confusion they have not resolved after several attempts and is still on the page.
criteria.false: The shopper is progressing normally or has already resolved the issue.

comparing.instructions: Is the shopper comparing this purchase with other stores right now?

criteria.true: Repeated tab blur/focus cycles around price or shipping information, or copying the product name or total.
criteria.false: No tab switching or copying; attention stays on the form.

hide.instructions: Rule: Hide posts written to make me angry or afraid so I react and share. Should this post be hidden under this rule?

criteria.true: The post is engineered to provoke outrage or fear: alarmist or exaggerated claims, an enemy to blame, urgency to share before it is removed, dehumanizing labels, or emotional bait with little verifiable information.
criteria.false: The post informs, asks, jokes, or shares a personal update. Serious or negative topics are fine when presented calmly, with sources or specifics, and without pressure to react or share.
